verses.text:
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt, saying,
“This month shall be the beginning of months for you; it shall be the first month of the year for you.
Speak to the whole congregation of the sons of Israel, saying: On the tenth day of this month, each shall take a sheep for the ancestral households, one sheep for each household.
If those in the house are too few to be sufficient for a sheep, he shall join with his nearest neighbour. According to the number of persons, each person’s sufficient portion shall be reckoned for the sheep.
Your sheep shall be without blemish, a male a year old; you shall take it from the lambs and from the young goats.
And you shall keep it until the fourteenth day of this month; and the whole multitude of the congregation of the sons of Israel shall slaughter it toward evening.
They shall take some of the blood and put it on the two doorposts and the lintel of the houses in which they eat them.
They shall eat the meat that night, roasted over fire, and eat unleavened bread with bitter herbs.
You shall eat none of it raw, nor boiled in water, but roasted with fire, its head together with its feet and inward parts.
You shall leave none of it until morning, and you shall not break a bone of it. Whatever remains until morning you shall burn with fire.
And this is how you shall eat it: your loins girded, your sandals upon your feet, and your staffs in your hands; and you shall eat it in haste. It is a Passover to the Lord.
I will go through the land of Egypt that night and strike every firstborn in the land of Egypt, both human and animal. Against all the Egyptians’ gods I will execute vengeance. I am the Lord.
And the blood shall be a sign to you upon the houses in which you are; and I will see the blood, and shelter you; and no plague of destruction shall be among you when I strike the land of Egypt.
This day shall be a memorial for you. You shall celebrate it as a feast to the Lord throughout all your generations; you shall celebrate it as a perpetual statute.

“Command the sons of Israel, saying, ‘See that you keep My Sabbaths, for they are a sign with Me and among you throughout your generations, that you may know that I am the Lord who sanctifies you.
You shall keep the Sabbaths, for this is holy to the Lord for you. Whoever profanes it shall surely be put to death. Whoever does work on it, that soul shall be destroyed from among his people.
For six days you shall do your work, but the seventh day is a Sabbath, a holy rest to the Lord. Whoever does work on the seventh day shall surely be put to death.
The sons of Israel shall keep the Sabbaths, observing them throughout their generations: an everlasting covenant.
It is an everlasting sign between Me and the sons of Israel, for in six days the Lord made heaven and earth, and on the seventh day He ceased and rested.’”

verses.text:
And if a man strikes another, and he dies, the one who struck him shall surely be put to death.
But if he did not act willingly, and God delivered him into his hands, I will give you a place where the slayer shall flee.
But if a man attacks his neighbour to kill him by deceit, and flees for refuge, you shall take him from My altar to put him to death.
He who strikes his father or his mother shall surely be put to death.
He who reviles his father or his mother shall surely die.
And if a man steals one of the sons of Israel, and overpowers him and sells him, and he is found with him, he shall surely die.
And if two men quarrel, and one strikes his neighbour with a stone or with his fist, and he does not die, but lies on his bed,
if the man rises and walks outside with a staff, the one who struck him shall be guiltless; only he shall pay for his lost labour and his healing.
And if a man strikes his male slave or his female slave with a rod, and the slave dies under his hands, he shall surely be avenged by judgment.
But if the slave survives a day or two, he shall not be avenged; for he is his silver.
And if two men fight and strike a woman with child, and her child comes out not fully formed, he shall surely be fined; as the woman’s husband shall impose on him, he shall pay according to an assessment.
But if it was fully formed, he shall give life for life,
eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
burn for burn, wound for wound, bruise for bruise.
And if a man strikes the eye of his household slave or of his female slave, and blinds it, he shall set them free for their eye.
And if he knocks out the tooth of his household slave or of his female slave, he shall set them free for their tooth.
And if a bull gores a man or a woman, and the person dies, the bull shall surely be stoned, and its flesh shall not be eaten; but the owner of the bull shall be guiltless.
But if the bull was in the habit of goring before, and its owner has been warned, and he does not remove it, and it kills a man or a woman, the bull shall be stoned, and its owner also shall die.
But if a ransom is imposed on him, he shall give for the ransom of his life all that they impose on him.
Whether it gores a son or a daughter, they shall deal with him according to this ordinance.
And if the bull gores a male slave or a female slave, he shall give thirty didrachmas of silver to their master, and the bull shall be stoned.
And if a man opens a pit, or hews out a pit, and does not cover it, and a calf or donkey falls in it,
the owner of the pit shall make restitution. He shall give silver to the animal’s owner, and the dead animal shall be his.
And if a man’s bull gores his neighbour’s bull, and it dies, they shall sell the living bull and divide its silver; and they shall also divide the dead bull.
But if the bull is known to have been in the habit of goring before, and its owner has been warned, and he does not remove it, he shall repay bull for bull; and the dead bull shall be his.

verses.text:
You shall make a lampstand of pure gold, of worked metal. Its stem, branches, bowls, knobs, and lilies shall be made from it.
Six branches shall extend from its sides, three from one side of the lampstand and three from the other.
There shall be three bowls shaped like little nuts, with a knob and lily on one branch. So it shall be for the six branches extending from the lampstand.
On the lampstand there shall be four bowls shaped like little nuts; on one branch shall be its knobs and lilies.
There shall be a knob under the two branches extending from it, and a knob under the four branches extending from it; so it shall be for the six branches extending from the lampstand.
Its knobs and branches shall be made from it, the whole worked from one piece of pure gold.

You shall make hair curtains as a covering over the tabernacle. You shall make eleven curtains.
Each curtain shall be thirty cubits long and four cubits wide. The eleven curtains shall have the same measure.
You shall join five hair curtains by themselves and six by themselves, and double over the sixth curtain at the front of the tabernacle.
You shall make fifty loops along the edge of the middle hair curtain at the joining, and fifty along the edge of the curtain joining the second set.
You shall make fifty clasps of bronze, and fasten the clasps into the loops, and join the hair curtains; and they shall be one.
You shall tuck under the surplus in the tabernacle’s hair curtains. You shall cover over the remaining half curtain; you shall cover over the surplus of the tabernacle’s hair curtains behind the tabernacle.
A cubit on this side and a cubit on that side, from the excess length of the tabernacle’s hair curtains, shall cover the tabernacle’s sides on either side.

You shall make each post ten cubits long, and the breadth of each post shall be a cubit and a half.
Each post shall have two tenons fitted opposite each other. You shall make all the tabernacle’s posts this way.
You shall make twenty posts for the tabernacle’s north side.
You shall make forty silver bases for the twenty posts, two bases for one post at its two parts, and two bases for another post at its two parts.
For the second side, to the south, there shall be twenty posts,
with their forty silver bases, two bases for one post at its two parts, and two bases for another post at its two parts.
For the rear of the tabernacle, toward the sea, you shall make six posts.
You shall make two posts for the corners at the rear of the tabernacle.
They shall be equal below, and likewise equal at their tops, at one joining. You shall make both this way for the two corners.
There shall be eight posts with sixteen silver bases, two for each post at its two parts, and two for each post.

verses.text:
You shall make a holy robe for Aaron your brother, for honour and glory.
Speak to everyone skilled in understanding whom I have filled with a spirit of perception. They shall make Aaron’s holy robe for the sanctuary, in which he shall serve Me as priest.
These are the robes they shall make: a breastpiece, a shoulder-piece, a full-length robe, a tasselled tunic, a turban, and a sash. They shall make holy robes for Aaron and his sons to serve Me as priests.
They shall take gold, blue, purple, scarlet yarn, and fine linen.
They shall make the shoulder-piece of spun fine linen, the work of a skilled weaving embroiderer.
It shall have two shoulder-pieces joined to one another, fitted at the two sides.
The woven work of the shoulder-pieces upon it shall be made as one piece with it, of the same workmanship: gold, blue, purple, spun scarlet yarn, and spun fine linen.

Connection to Christ: Hebrews supplies a broad sanctuary-to-Christ connection, while James describes anointing the sick; neither turns this recipe into a universal Christian formula. Christian response today: Treat worship reverently and distinguish Israel’s reserved oil from other legitimate uses of oil.
Full research entry

verses.text:
The Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
“Take spices: five hundred shekels of the choicest myrrh, half as much fragrant cinnamon, two hundred and fifty, and two hundred and fifty of fragrant cane,
five hundred sanctuary shekels of iris, and a hin of olive oil.
Make these into holy anointing oil, a compound prepared by a perfumer’s skill. It shall be holy anointing oil.
With it anoint the Tent of Testimony and the ark of the testimony,
the lampstand and all its utensils, and the incense altar,
the altar of whole burnt offerings and all its utensils, the table and all its utensils, and the basin and its base.
Consecrate them, and they shall be most holy. Everyone who touches them shall be sanctified.
Anoint Aaron and his sons and consecrate them to serve Me as priests.
Tell the sons of Israel: ‘This shall be holy anointing oil for you throughout your generations.
It shall not be applied to human flesh, and you shall not make anything like it for yourselves according to this composition. It is holy and shall be a holy thing to you.
Whoever makes anything like it, or gives any of it to an outsider, shall be destroyed from among his people.’”

The Lord said to Moses, “Take to yourself spices: stacte, onycha, fragrant galbanum, and clear frankincense, in equal portions.

Whoever makes anything like it to enjoy its fragrance shall perish from among his people.”

verses.text:
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying,
If a soul sins, and utterly disregards the commandments of the Lord, and deals falsely with his neighbour concerning a deposit, or a partnership, or robbery, or any wrong which he has done unto his neighbour,
or finds a lost thing and deals falsely concerning it, and swears unjustly concerning any of all the things which a man may do so as to sin therein,
then it shall be, when he has sinned and incurred guilt, that he shall return the plunder which he seized, or that which he obtained by wrong, or the deposit which was entrusted unto him, or the lost thing which he found,
concerning every matter about which he swore unjustly. And he shall repay the principal, and add a fifth part unto it; he shall repay it unto the one to whom it belongs, on the day when he is convicted.
And for his offence he shall bring unto the Lord an unblemished ram from the flock, of a value corresponding to the offence which he has committed against Him.
And the priest shall make atonement for him before the Lord, and he shall be forgiven concerning any of all the things which he has done and wherein he has offended Him.

title: Israel’s distinctions between clean and unclean food
audience_note: Shared instruction or study teaching. Read the original audience, conditions and existing classification before applying it.
paragraphs: Audience: Shared instruction or study teaching. Read the original audience, conditions and existing classification before applying it.
Classification: Study context · Topical study
Topic: Food, ritual purity and cleansing

Connection to Christ: Jesus, Acts and Romans address defilement, food and conscience; Christian interpretations of their relationship to Leviticus differ. Christian response today: Receive food with thanksgiving, pursue purity of heart, avoid idolatry and refuse to pressure or despise another believer over food; keep Acts 15’s instructions in view.

verses.text:
And the Lord spoke unto Moses and Aaron, saying:
Speak to the sons of Israel, saying: These are the animals you may eat among all the animals on the earth.
Every animal among the livestock that divides the hoof, and cleaves its claws into two hoofs, and brings up the cud: these you may eat.
Nevertheless, of these you shall not eat: among those that bring up the cud and those that divide the hoof and cleave the claws, the camel, because it brings up the cud, but does not divide the hoof; it is unclean unto you;
and the hare, because it brings up the cud but does not divide the hoof; it is unclean for you;
and the choirogryllios, because it brings up the cud but does not divide the hoof; it is unclean for you;
and the pig, because it divides the hoof and has cleft hoof-claws but does not bring up the cud; it is unclean for you.
You shall not eat their flesh or touch their carcasses; they are unclean for you.
And these you may eat among all that are in the waters: whatever has fins and scales in the waters, in the seas and streams, you may eat.
And whatever has neither fins nor scales in the water, in the seas and streams, among all that the waters bring forth and every living creature in the water, is an abomination.
And they shall be abominations for you. You shall not eat their flesh, and you shall abhor their carcasses.
And whatever among the things in the water has no fins and scales is an abomination for you.
And these you shall abhor among the birds; they shall not be eaten, for they are an abomination: the eagle, the gryps, and the sea-eagle;
and the vulture, the kite, and those like it;
and the raven and those like it;
and the ostrich, the owl, the gull and those like it, and the hawk and those like it;
and the night-raven, the diving bird, and the ibis;
and the purple waterbird, the pelican, and the swan;
and the owl, the heron, the plover and those like it, the hoopoe, and the bat.
And every winged creeping thing that walks on four is an abomination for you.
But among the winged creeping things that walk on four, you may eat those that have legs above their feet for leaping on the earth.
And these among them you may eat: the brouchos and those like it, the attakes and those like it, the locust and those like it, and the snake-fighter and those like it.
Every winged creeping thing that has four feet is an abomination for you.
And by these you shall become defiled: everyone who touches their carcasses shall be unclean until evening,
and whosoever carries any of their carcasses shall wash his garments and be unclean until evening.
Every animal that divides the hoof and has cleft claws but does not chew the cud shall be unclean for you. Whosoever touches their carcasses shall be unclean until evening.
And among all wild animals that walk on four, whatever walks on its hands shall be unclean for you. Whosoever touches their carcasses shall be unclean until evening.
And whosoever carries their carcasses shall wash his garments and be unclean until evening. They are unclean for you.
And these are unclean for you among the creeping things that creep on the earth: the weasel, the mouse, and the land crocodile;
the shrew, the chameleon, the spotted lizard, the lizard, and the mole.
These are unclean for you among all the creeping things on the earth. Whosoever touches them when they are dead shall be unclean until evening.
And anything on which one of them falls when dead shall become unclean: any wooden utensil, garment, skin, or sack, any article used for work. It shall be dipped in water and remain unclean until evening; then it shall be clean.
And if one of them falls inside any earthenware vessel, everything in it shall become unclean, and the vessel shall be shattered.
And any food that may be eaten, on which water comes, shall become unclean, and any drink that may be drunk in any vessel shall become unclean.
And anything on which any of their carcasses falls shall become unclean. Ovens and pot-stands shall be demolished; these are unclean and shall be unclean for you.
But springs of water, a cistern, and a gathering of water shall remain clean; whosoever touches their carcasses shall be unclean.
If any of their carcasses falls on seed intended for sowing, it remains clean.
But if water is poured on any seed and any of their carcasses falls on it, it is unclean for you.
If an animal that you may eat dies, whosoever touches its carcass shall be unclean until evening.
And whosoever eats from these carcasses shall wash his garments and be unclean until evening. Whosoever carries any of their carcasses shall wash his garments, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
And every creeping thing that creeps upon the earth shall be an abomination for you; it shall not be eaten.
And whatever moves on its belly, whatever walks on four continually, whatever has many feet among all the creeping things that creep upon the earth, you shall not eat, for it is an abomination for you.
And you shall in no wise make your souls abominable through any creeping things that creep upon the earth; neither shall you be defiled through them, nor shall you be unclean through them;
for I am the Lord your God; and you shall be sanctified and you shall be holy, for I am holy, the Lord your God. And you shall not defile your souls through any creeping things that move upon the earth;
for I am the Lord who brought you up out of the land of Egypt to be your God; and you shall be holy, for I am holy, the Lord.
This is the law concerning animals, birds, every creature that moves in the water, and every creature that creeps upon the earth,
to distinguish between the unclean and the clean, and between the living creatures that are eaten and the living creatures that are not eaten.

verses.text:
You shall eat no abominable thing.
These are the beasts which you may eat: a calf of the cattle, and a lamb of the sheep, and a young male goat of the goats,
deer, gazelle, bubalos, goat-stag, white-rumped antelope, oryx, and giraffe.
Every beast that divides the hoof, and cleaves its hoof into two parts, and brings up the cud among the beasts, these you may eat.
And these you shall not eat of those that bring up the cud, and of those that divide the hoof and cleave its parts: the camel, and the hare, and the rock hyrax; for they bring up the cud, but do not divide the hoof; they are unclean unto you.
And the swine, for it divides the hoof and cleaves its parts, but does not chew the cud, is unclean unto you. Of their flesh you shall not eat, neither shall you touch their carcasses.

verses.text:
And the Lord spoke unto Moses and Aaron, saying:
If anyone has on the skin of his body a bright scar-like mark, and it becomes a lesion of leprosy on his skin, he shall be brought unto Aaron the priest or to one of his sons, the priests.
And the priest shall examine the lesion on the skin of his body. If the hair in the lesion has turned white and the lesion appears lower than the skin of his body, it is a lesion of leprosy. The priest shall examine him and declare him unclean.
If the bright spot on his skin is white but does not appear lower than the skin, and its hair has not turned white, but it is faint, the priest shall isolate the lesion for seven days.
And the priest shall examine the lesion on the seventh day; and, behold, if the lesion remains before him, and the lesion has not shifted in the skin, the priest shall isolate him for a second seven days.
And the priest shall examine him on the seventh day a second time; and, behold, if the lesion is faint, and the lesion has not shifted in the skin, the priest shall declare him clean, for it is a mark; and having washed his garments, he shall be clean.
But if the mark changes and shifts in the skin after the priest has examined him for cleansing, he shall appear before the priest a second time,
and the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if the mark has shifted in the skin, the priest shall declare him unclean; it is leprosy.

verses.text:
And the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if there is a white scar in the skin, and it has turned the hair white, and there is some sound living flesh in the scar,
it is longstanding leprosy on the skin of his body. The priest shall declare him unclean and isolate him, for he is unclean.
But if the leprosy breaks out abundantly in the skin, and the leprosy covers all the skin of the lesion from head to foot, throughout the whole view of the priest,
the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if the leprosy has covered all the skin of his body, the priest shall declare him clean as to the lesion, because it has all turned white; it is clean.
And on whatever day living skin appears on him, he shall be defiled.
And the priest shall examine the sound skin, and the sound skin shall make him unclean, because it is unclean; it is leprosy.
But if the sound skin is restored and turns white, he shall come unto the priest,
and the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if the lesion has turned white, the priest shall declare the lesion clean; he is clean.

Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: If any man has a flow from his body, his flow is unclean.
And this is the law of his uncleanness: discharging seed from his body through the flow by which his body has become stopped up, this is his uncleanness in him; all the days of the flow of his body, in which his body has become stopped up through the flow, are his uncleanness.

and everything on which she lies during her menstrual discharge shall be unclean, and everything on which she sits shall be unclean.

verses.text:
If anyone lies with her and her uncleanness comes upon him, he shall be unclean for seven days, and every bed on which he lies shall be unclean.
And if a woman has a flow of blood for many days outside the time of her menstrual discharge, or if she also has a flow after her menstrual discharge, all the days of her unclean flow shall be like the days of her menstrual discharge; she shall be unclean.
And every bed on which she lies during all the days of her flow shall be like the bed of her menstrual discharge, and every article on which she sits shall be unclean, as in the uncleanness of her menstrual discharge.

And if a woman has a flow of blood, her flow shall be in her body; she shall remain in her menstrual discharge for seven days. Whosoever touches her shall be unclean until evening,
and everything on which she lies during her menstrual discharge shall be unclean, and everything on which she sits shall be unclean.
And whosoever touches her bed shall wash his garments, bathe his body in water, and be unclean until evening.
And whosoever touches any article on which she sits shall wash his garments, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
If, while she is on her bed or on the article on which she sits, he touches her, he shall be unclean until evening.

verses.text:
Say unto Aaron: A man from your kin throughout your generations, in whom there is a blemish, shall not draw near to present the gifts of his God.
No man who has a blemish shall approach: a lame man, a blind man, one with a mutilated nose, or one with a cut-off ear;
or a man with a broken hand or a broken foot;
or a hunchback, one with a skin spot, one with diseased eyelids, a man with a severe scab or skin eruption, or one with a single testicle.
No one of the seed of Aaron the priest, in whom there is a blemish, shall draw near to present the sacrifices unto your God; because a blemish is in him, he shall not draw near to present the gifts of God.
He may eat the gifts of God, both the most holy things and portions of the holy things.
But he shall not approach the veil or come near the altar, because he has a blemish. He shall not profane the holy place of his God, for I am the Lord who sanctifies them.

verses.text:
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Say unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: When you enter the land which I give unto you, and reap its harvest, you shall bring a sheaf as the first portion of your harvest unto the priest;
and he shall offer up the sheaf before the Lord, acceptable for you; the priest shall offer it up on the morrow after the first day.
And on the day you bring the sheaf, you shall offer an unblemished year-old sheep as a whole burnt offering unto the Lord.
And its sacrifice shall be two tenths of fine flour kneaded with oil, a sacrifice unto the Lord, a sweet savour unto the Lord. Its drink offering shall be a quarter of a hin of wine.
And you shall eat neither bread nor roasted fresh grain until that very day, until you bring the gifts to your God. This is an everlasting ordinance throughout your generations in every dwelling of yours.
And you shall count from the day after the Sabbath, from the day you bring the sheaf of the presentation, seven complete weeks.
Until the day after the last week you shall count fifty days, and then present a new sacrifice unto the Lord.
From your dwelling you shall bring bread as a presentation, two loaves. They shall be made from two tenths of fine flour and baked leavened, as firstfruits unto the Lord.
And with the loaves you shall bring seven unblemished year-old lambs, one calf from the herd, and two unblemished rams. They shall be a whole burnt offering unto the Lord, with their sacrifices and drink offerings, a sacrifice, a sweet savour unto the Lord.
And they shall offer one male young goat from the goats for sin and two year-old lambs as a sacrifice of deliverance with the firstfruits loaves.
And the priest shall present them with the firstfruits loaves as a presentation before the Lord, with the two lambs. They shall be holy unto the Lord; they shall belong unto the priest who presents them.
And you shall proclaim this day a convocation; it shall be holy for you. You shall do no laborious work on it. This is an everlasting ordinance throughout your generations in every dwelling of yours.
And when you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not finish the remainder of the harvest of your field when you reap; neither shall you gather what falls from your harvest; you shall leave them for the poor and for the resident foreigner; I am the Lord your God.

verses.text:
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Speak to the sons of Israel, saying: On the fifteenth day of this seventh month is the Feast of Tents unto the Lord for seven days.
And on the first day there shall be a holy convocation. You shall do no laborious work.
For seven days you shall bring whole burnt offerings unto the Lord. The eighth day shall be a holy convocation for you, and you shall bring whole burnt offerings unto the Lord. It is a closing observance; you shall do no laborious work.
These are the feasts for the Lord, which you shall proclaim as holy convocations, to present offerings unto the Lord: whole burnt offerings and their sacrifices and their drink offerings, each day’s requirement on its day,
besides the Lord’s Sabbaths, besides your gifts, besides all your vows, and besides your freewill offerings that you give unto the Lord.
And on the fifteenth day of this seventh month, when you finish gathering the produce of the land, you shall celebrate unto the Lord for seven days. On the first day there shall be rest, and on the eighth day there shall be rest.
And on the first day you shall take beautiful fruit of a tree, and palm fronds, and dense branches of a tree, and willows, and branches of the chaste tree from a stream, to rejoice before the Lord your God seven days
of the year. This is an everlasting ordinance throughout your generations; you shall celebrate it in the seventh month.
You shall dwell in tents seven days; every native in Israel shall dwell in tents,
so that your generations may see that I made the sons of Israel dwell in tents when I brought them out of the land of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.

And also offer one male goat for sin, besides the continual whole burning, their sacrifices, and their drink offerings.

verses.text:
And you shall count unto yourself seven rests of years, seven years seven times; and the seven weeks of years shall be unto you forty-nine years.
And you shall make proclamation with a trumpet sound throughout your land in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month. On the Day of Atonement you shall make proclamation with a trumpet throughout your land.
And you shall consecrate the fiftieth year, and proclaim release throughout the land unto all who dwell therein; this shall be a year of release, a signal unto you; and each one shall depart unto his possession, and each of you shall depart unto his ancestral homeland.
This is a signal of release: the fiftieth year shall be a year for you. You shall not sow, reap what grows of itself, or gather its consecrated produce.
For it is a signal of release; it shall be holy to you. You shall eat its produce from the fields.
In the year of release, at its signal, each shall return to his possession.
But if one sells property unto your neighbour, or you acquire it from your neighbour, let no man oppress his neighbour.
According to the number of years after the signal you shall acquire from your neighbour; according to the number of harvest years he shall sell to you.
As the years increase, you shall increase its purchase price; as the years decrease, you shall decrease its purchase price, for he is selling you a number of harvests.
Let no man oppress his neighbour, and you shall fear the Lord your God; I am the Lord your God.

But if anyone sells a dwelling house in a walled city, its redemption shall be possible until a year of days is fulfilled; that shall be its redemption period.
If it is not redeemed before its whole year is complete, the house in the city that has a wall shall be confirmed permanently to its buyer throughout his generations. It shall not go out at the release.
But houses in settlements that have no surrounding wall shall be reckoned with the field of the land. They shall always be redeemable and shall go out at the release.

Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: Whosoever vows a vow for the valuation of his soul unto the Lord,
the valuation of a male from twenty to sixty years old shall be fifty didrachmas of silver, by the sacred weight.
For a female the assessed value shall be thirty didrachmas.
From five to twenty years old, the valuation shall be twenty didrachmas for a male and ten didrachmas for a female.
From one month to five years old, the valuation shall be five didrachmas of silver for a male and three didrachmas for a female.
From sixty years old and upward, the valuation shall be fifteen didrachmas of silver for a male and ten didrachmas for a female.
But if he is too poor for the valuation, he shall stand before the priest, and the priest shall value him; the priest shall value him according to the strength of the hand of the one who vowed.

verse_units.text: And the sons of Israel shall camp, each in his own formation and each according to his own command, with their army.

verses.text:
Let the sons of Israel camp, each beside his neighbour, by formation and by the signs of their ancestral houses. The sons of Israel shall camp opposite, around the Tent of Testimony.
And those camping first toward the east shall be the formation of Judah’s camp, with their army. The ruler of the sons of Judah is Nahshon son of Amminadab.
His army, those registered, numbered seventy-four thousand six hundred.
And those camping next shall be the tribe of Issachar; the ruler of the sons of Issachar is Nethanel son of Zuar.
His army, those registered, numbered fifty-four thousand four hundred.
And those camping next shall be the tribe of Zebulun; the ruler of the sons of Zebulun is Eliab son of Helon.
His army, those registered, numbered fifty-seven thousand four hundred.
All those registered in the camp of Judah, with their army, numbered one hundred eighty-six thousand four hundred. They shall set out first.
The formation of the camp of Reuben, with their army, shall be toward the southwest. The ruler of the sons of Reuben is Elizur son of Shedeur.
His army, those registered, numbered forty-six thousand five hundred.
And those camping next shall be the tribe of Simeon; the ruler of the sons of Simeon is Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.
His army, those registered, numbered fifty-nine thousand three hundred.
And those camping next shall be the tribe of Gad; the ruler of the sons of Gad is Eliasaph son of Reuel.
His army, those registered, numbered forty-five thousand six hundred fifty.
All those registered in the camp of Reuben, with their army, numbered one hundred fifty-one thousand four hundred fifty. They shall set out second.
And the Tent of Testimony and the camp of the Levites shall be raised in the middle of the camps. As they camp, so they shall set out, each beside his neighbour according to command.
The formation of the camp of Ephraim, with their army, shall be toward the sea. The ruler of the sons of Ephraim is Elishama son of Ammihud.
His army, those registered, numbered forty thousand five hundred.
And those camping next shall be the tribe of Manasseh; the ruler of the sons of Manasseh is Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.
His army, those registered, numbered thirty-two thousand two hundred.
And those camping next shall be the tribe of Benjamin; the ruler of the sons of Benjamin is Abidan son of Gideoni.
His army, those registered, numbered thirty-five thousand four hundred.
All those registered in the camp of Ephraim, with their army, numbered one hundred eight thousand one hundred. They shall set out third.
The formation of the camp of Dan, with their army, shall be toward the north. The ruler of the sons of Dan is Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.
His army, those registered, numbered sixty-two thousand seven hundred.
And those camping next shall be the tribe of Asher; the ruler of the sons of Asher is Pagiel son of Ocran.
His army, those registered, numbered forty-one thousand five hundred.
And those camping next shall be the tribe of Naphtali; the ruler of the sons of Naphtali is Ahira son of Enan.
His army, those registered, numbered fifty-three thousand four hundred.
All those registered in the camp of Dan numbered one hundred fifty-seven thousand six hundred. They shall set out last, by their formation.

verses.text:
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: If a man or woman solemnly vows a vow of consecration unto the Lord, to be set apart
from wine and strong drink, he shall be purified from wine. He shall drink neither vinegar of wine, nor vinegar of strong drink, nor anything prepared from grapes; and he shall eat neither fresh grapes nor raisins.
All the days of his vow he shall consume nothing made from the vine: wine, from pressed grape skins unto the seed.
All the days of the vow of purification no razor shall come upon his head. Until the days which he vowed unto the Lord are fulfilled, he shall be holy, letting the hair of his head grow long.
All the days of his vow unto the Lord he shall not enter where any dead person is.
For his father, or his mother, or his brother, or his sister, he shall not defile himself when they die; for the vow of his God is upon him, upon his head.
All the days of his vow he shall be holy unto the Lord.
But if anyone dies suddenly beside him, the head of his vow shall be defiled forthwith. He shall shave his head on the day when he is cleansed; on the seventh day it shall be shaved.
And on the eighth day he shall bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons unto the priest, at the doors of the Tent of Testimony.
And the priest shall prepare one for sin and one for a whole burnt offering. And the priest shall make atonement for him concerning his sin in connection with the dead person, and shall consecrate his head on that day,
whereon he was consecrated unto the Lord for the days of the vow. And he shall bring a year-old lamb for a guilt offering; and the former days shall not be reckoned, for the head of his vow was defiled.
And this is the law of him who has vowed: on the day when he fulfils the days of his vow, he shall present his offering at the doors of the Tent of Testimony,
and he shall bring his gift unto the Lord: one unblemished year-old male lamb for whole burning, and one unblemished year-old ewe lamb for sin, and one unblemished ram for deliverance,
and a basket of unleavened bread of fine flour, loaves prepared with oil, and unleavened wafers spread with oil, and their sacrifice and their drink offering.
And the priest shall present them before the Lord, and prepare his offering for sin and his whole burnt offering.
And he shall prepare the ram as a sacrifice of deliverance unto the Lord, with the basket of unleavened bread; and the priest shall prepare its sacrifice and its drink offering.
And he who has vowed shall shave the head of his vow at the doors of the Tent of Testimony, and put the hair upon the fire which is under the sacrifice of deliverance.
And the priest shall take the boiled foreleg from the ram, and one unleavened loaf from the basket, and one unleavened wafer, and put them upon the hands of him who has vowed, after he has shaved the hair of his vow.
And the priest shall bring them as a presentation before the Lord. It shall be holy unto the priest, with the breast of presentation and the foreleg of the portion set apart; and afterward he who has vowed shall drink wine.
This is the law of him who vows unto the Lord, his gift unto the Lord concerning the vow, apart from whatever his hand may find, according to the extent of his vow which he vows under the law of consecration.

verses.text:
By the command of the Lord the sons of Israel shall camp, and by the command of the Lord they shall set out; all the days in which the cloud overshadows the Tent, the sons of Israel shall camp.
And when the cloud remains over the Tent for many days, the sons of Israel shall keep the charge of God, and shall in no wise set out.
And it shall be, when the cloud covers the Tent for a number of days, that by the voice of the Lord they shall camp, and by the command of the Lord they shall set out.
And it shall be, when the cloud remains from evening until morning, and the cloud rises in the morning, that they shall set out by day or by night.
For the days of a month, while the cloud continues overshadowing it, the sons of Israel shall camp, and shall in no wise set out.
For by the command of the Lord they shall set out. They kept the Lord’s charge, by the command of the Lord through Moses.

wording_notes: This is the cited study context; the record does not identify a separate primary command passage.

verses.text:
Whosoever touches a dead person, any human being who has died, shall be unclean for seven days.
That person shall be purified on the third day and on the seventh day, and he shall be clean. If he is not purified on the third day and on the seventh day, he shall not be clean.
Whosoever touches the dead body of any human being who has died, and is not purified, has defiled the Tent of the Lord; that soul shall be wiped out from Israel. Because water of sprinkling was not sprinkled upon him, he is unclean; his uncleanness is still in him.
And this is the law: If a person dies in a house, everyone who enters the house and everything in the house shall be unclean for seven days.
And every open vessel without a fastening tied upon it is unclean.
And anyone who touches, on the open plain, one slain, a dead person, a human bone, or a tomb shall be unclean for seven days.
And for the unclean person they shall take some ashes from what was burned for purification, and they shall pour living water over them into a vessel.
And a clean man shall take hyssop, dip it in the water, and sprinkle it around the house, the vessels, and the people who were there, and on whoever touched the human bone, the slain person, the dead person, or the tomb.
And the clean person shall sprinkle the unclean person on the third day and on the seventh day. He shall be purified on the seventh day, wash his clothes, and bathe in water, and he shall be unclean until evening.
And if a man is defiled, and is not purified, that soul shall be destroyed from the midst of the congregation, because he has defiled the holy things of the Lord; because water of sprinkling was not sprinkled upon him, he is unclean.
And this shall be an everlasting ordinance for you. The one who sprinkles the water of sprinkling shall wash his clothes, and whosoever touches the water of sprinkling shall be unclean until evening.
And whatever the unclean person touches shall be unclean, and the person who touches it shall be unclean until evening.

verses.text:
And the daughters of Zelophehad son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, of the clan of Manasseh among the sons of Joseph, came forward. Their names were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
And they stood before Moses, Eleazar the priest, the rulers, and the whole congregation at the entrance of the Tent of Testimony, saying:
Our father died in the wilderness. He was not among the congregation that rose against the Lord in Korah's congregation; he died because of his own sin, and he had no sons.
Let our father's name not be erased from his clan because he has no son. Give us a possession among our father's brothers.
And Moses brought their case before the Lord.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
The daughters of Zelophehad have spoken rightly. You shall surely give them a possession of inheritance among their father’s brethren, and shall assign their father’s allotment unto them.
And you shall speak unto the sons of Israel, saying: If a man dies, and has no son, you shall assign his inheritance unto his daughter.
But if he has no daughter, you shall give the inheritance to his brother.
But if he has no brothers, you shall give the inheritance to his father's brother.
But if his father has no brothers, you shall give the inheritance to his nearest relative from his tribe, and he shall inherit his property. This shall be a rule of judgment for the sons of Israel, as the Lord commanded Moses.

and her father hears her vows and her restrictions that she imposed upon herself, but her father remains silent toward her, then all her vows shall stand, and all her restrictions that she imposed upon herself shall remain.
But if her father refuses her on the day he hears, none of her vows or restrictions that she imposed upon herself shall stand. The Lord will cleanse her, because her father refused her.
If she becomes a man’s wife while her vows are upon her, according to the specific statement of her lips by which she imposed a restriction upon herself,
and her husband hears, and remains silent toward her on the day he hears, then all her vows shall stand, and her restrictions that she imposed upon herself shall remain.
But if her husband refuses her on the day he hears, none of her vows or restrictions that she imposed upon herself shall remain, because her husband refused her. The Lord will cleanse her.
And the vow of a widow or a divorced woman—whatever she vowed concerning herself—shall remain against her.
If her vow was made in her husband’s house, or her restriction was imposed upon herself with an oath,
and her husband hears, and remains silent toward her, and does not refuse her, then all her vows shall stand, and all her restrictions which she imposed upon her soul shall stand against her.
But if her husband utterly annuls them on the day he hears, then whatever came from her lips concerning her vows and the restrictions upon herself shall not remain against her. Her husband has annulled them, and the Lord will cleanse her.
Every vow and every oath imposing a restriction to afflict her soul—her husband may establish it, or her husband may annul it.
But if he remains utterly silent toward her from day to day, he shall establish all her vows, and he shall establish the restrictions upon her, because he kept silence toward her on the day when he heard.
But if he annuls them after the day on which he heard, he shall bear his sin.
These are the ordinances that the Lord commanded Moses between a man and his wife, and between a father and his daughter in her youth in her father’s house.

verses.text:
Command the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: You are entering the land of Canaan; this shall be your inheritance, the land of Canaan with its boundaries.
And your southwestern side shall run from the wilderness of Sin to the territory adjoining Edom. Your southwestern boundary shall begin from the part of the Salt Sea toward the east.
And the boundary shall turn around you from the southwest toward the Ascent of Akrabin and pass through Senna. Its endpoint shall be southwest of Kadesh-barnea; it shall extend to the settlement of Arad and pass through Azmon.
And the boundary shall turn from Azmon to the Wadi of Egypt, and its endpoint shall be the sea.
And for your sea boundary, the Great Sea shall mark the limit. This shall be your sea boundary.
And this shall be your boundary toward the north: from the Great Sea you shall measure out for yourselves beside the mountain, the mountain;
and from the mountain, the mountain, you shall measure out for them toward the entrance into Hamath; and its endpoint shall be the boundaries of Sarada.
And the boundary shall extend to Dephrona, and its endpoint shall be Hazar-enan. This shall be your northern boundary.
And you shall measure out for yourselves the eastern boundary from Hazar-enan unto Shepham.
And the boundary shall descend from Shepham to Arbela, from the east toward the springs. The boundary shall descend to Bela, along the eastern ridge of the Sea of Chennara.
And the boundary shall descend to the Jordan, and its endpoint shall be the Salt Sea. This shall be your land and its surrounding boundaries.

verses.text:
Instruct the sons of Israel to give the Levites towns to live in from their allotted possessions. They shall also give the Levites the outlying lands around the towns.
And the towns shall be theirs to live in, and their designated lands shall be for their livestock and all their four-footed animals.
And the lands adjoining the towns that you shall give the Levites shall extend two thousand cubits outward from the town wall all around.
And you shall measure outside the town two thousand cubits on the eastern side, and two thousand cubits on the southwestern side, and two thousand cubits on the seaward side, and two thousand cubits on the northern side; and the town shall be in the midst thereof for you, together with the adjoining lands of the towns.
And you shall give the Levites the six cities of refuge that you shall provide for the person who has killed someone to flee to, and in addition to these, forty-two towns.
All the towns you shall give the Levites shall be forty-eight towns, together with their outlying lands.
And for the towns that you shall give from the possession of the sons of Israel, take many from those with much and fewer from those with less. Each shall give towns to the Levites according to the inheritance he receives.

verse_units.text: Take heed unto yourself, lest you forget the Lord your God, and fail to keep His commandments, and His judgments, and His ordinances which I command you this day;
lest, when you have eaten and are filled, and have built good houses and dwelt in them,
and your herds and your flocks are multiplied, and your silver and your gold are multiplied, and all that you have is multiplied,
you become lifted up in heart, and forget the Lord your God, who brought you forth out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage;

who led you through that great and fearful wilderness, wherein were biting serpents, and scorpions, and thirst, where there was no water; who brought forth for you a spring of water out of the sheer rock;
who fed you with manna in the wilderness, which your fathers did not know, to afflict you and to test you, and to do you good in your latter days.
Do not say in your heart: My strength and the might of my hand have gotten me this great wealth.
And you shall remember the Lord your God, for He gives you strength to gain wealth, that He may establish His covenant which the Lord sware unto your fathers, as at this day.

Classification: Study context · Topical study

Connection to Christ: Jesus and Paul address food and defilement; Christians interpret their relationship to Israel’s food distinctions differently. Christian response today: Practice purity of heart and grateful eating, avoid idolatry, and protect fellowship and conscience rather than turning dietary choices into a measure of another person’s worth.
Full research entry
wording_notes: This is the cited study context; the record does not identify a separate primary command passage.

verses.text:
You shall eat no abominable thing.
These are the beasts which you may eat: a calf of the cattle, and a lamb of the sheep, and a young male goat of the goats,
deer, gazelle, bubalos, goat-stag, white-rumped antelope, oryx, and giraffe.
Every beast that divides the hoof, and cleaves its hoof into two parts, and brings up the cud among the beasts, these you may eat.
And these you shall not eat of those that bring up the cud, and of those that divide the hoof and cleave its parts: the camel, and the hare, and the rock hyrax; for they bring up the cud, but do not divide the hoof; they are unclean unto you.
And the swine, for it divides the hoof and cleaves its parts, but does not chew the cud, is unclean unto you. Of their flesh you shall not eat, neither shall you touch their carcasses.
And these you may eat of all that are in the waters: whatsoever has fins and scales, you may eat.
And whatsoever does not have fins and scales, you shall not eat; they are unclean unto you.
Every clean bird you may eat.
And these you shall not eat of them: the eagle, and the griffon vulture, and the sea-eagle,
and the vulture, and the kite, and those like it,
and every raven, and those like it,
and the ostrich, and the owl, and the gull,
and the heron, and the swan, and the ibis,
and the diving bird, and the hawk, and those like it, and the hoopoe, and the night-raven,
and the pelican, and the plover, and those like it, and the purple swamphen, and the bat.
All creeping things among the flying creatures are unclean unto you; you shall not eat of them.
Every clean flying creature you may eat.

You shall surely tithe all the produce of your seed, the yield of your field, year by year.

Full research entry
wording_notes: This is the cited study context; the record does not identify a separate primary command passage.

verses.text:
At the end of seven years you shall make a release.
And this is the ordinance of the release: you shall release every debt of yours which your neighbour owes you; and you shall not exact it of your brother, for a release unto the Lord your God has been proclaimed.
Of a foreigner you may exact whatsoever he owes you; but you shall release your brother’s debt unto you.
For there shall be none in need among you; for the Lord your God shall surely bless you in the land which the Lord your God gives you for a possession, to inherit it,
if you diligently hearken unto the voice of the Lord your God, to keep and do all these commandments which I command you this day.
For the Lord your God has blessed you, as He has spoken unto you; and you shall lend unto many nations, but you shall not borrow; and you shall rule over many nations, but they shall not rule over you.
And if there is among you one of your brethren in need, within any of your cities in the land which the Lord your God gives you, you shall not withhold the affection of your heart, neither shall you close your hand against your needy brother.
You shall freely open your hands unto him, and shall surely lend him as much as he needs, according to his want.
Take heed unto yourself, lest there be a hidden, lawless thought in your heart, saying: The seventh year, the year of release, draws near; and your eye be evil toward your needy brother, and you give him nothing, and he cry against you unto the Lord, and there be great sin upon you.
You shall freely give unto him, and shall surely lend him as much as he needs; and your heart shall not be grieved when you give unto him. For because of this the Lord your God shall bless you in all your works, and in all that you put your hand unto.
For the needy shall never cease out of the land; therefore I command you to do this thing, saying: You shall freely open your hands unto your poor brother and unto the needy in your land.
And if your brother, a Hebrew man or a Hebrew woman, is sold unto you, he shall serve you six years; and in the seventh year you shall send him forth free from you.
And when you send him forth free from you, you shall not send him away empty.
You shall furnish him generously out of your sheep, and out of your grain, and out of your winepress; as the Lord your God has blessed you, you shall give unto him.
And you shall remember that you were a household slave in the land of Egypt, and the Lord your God redeemed you thence; therefore I command you to do this thing.
And if he says unto you: I will not go forth from you, because he loves you and your house, and because it is well with him beside you,
then you shall take an awl, and pierce his ear against the door, and he shall be your household slave for ever; and unto your female slave you shall do likewise.
It shall not seem hard unto you when they are sent forth free from you, for he served you six years for the yearly wage of a hired worker; and the Lord your God shall bless you in all that you do.

verses.text:
And if there is among you one of your brethren in need, within any of your cities in the land which the Lord your God gives you, you shall not withhold the affection of your heart, neither shall you close your hand against your needy brother.
You shall freely open your hands unto him, and shall surely lend him as much as he needs, according to his want.
Take heed unto yourself, lest there be a hidden, lawless thought in your heart, saying: The seventh year, the year of release, draws near; and your eye be evil toward your needy brother, and you give him nothing, and he cry against you unto the Lord, and there be great sin upon you.
You shall freely give unto him, and shall surely lend him as much as he needs; and your heart shall not be grieved when you give unto him. For because of this the Lord your God shall bless you in all your works, and in all that you put your hand unto.
For the needy shall never cease out of the land; therefore I command you to do this thing, saying: You shall freely open your hands unto your poor brother and unto the needy in your land.

And if a man has two wives, one loved and one hated, and both the loved and the hated bear him children, and the firstborn son is hers that is hated,
then it shall be, in the day when he gives his sons an inheritance of his possessions, that he may not make the son of the loved wife the firstborn, overlooking the firstborn son of the hated wife.
But he shall acknowledge the firstborn, the son of the hated wife, by giving him a double portion of all that he has; for he is the beginning of his children, and the right of the firstborn belongs unto him.

verses.text:
And if brethren dwell together, and one of them dies, and has no seed, the wife of the dead shall not be married outside unto a man who is not near of kin. Her husband’s brother shall go in unto her, and take her unto himself for a wife, and dwell with her as husband.
And it shall be, that the child whom she bears shall be established in the name of the dead, and his name shall not be blotted out of Israel.
And if the man will not take his brother’s wife, the woman shall go up unto the gate, unto the elders, and say: My husband’s brother will not raise up his brother’s name in Israel; my husband’s brother has refused.
And the elders of his city shall call him, and speak unto him; and if he stands and says: I will not take her,
then his brother’s wife shall draw near before the elders, and loose one sandal from his foot, and spit in his face, and answer and say: Thus shall they do unto the man who will not build up his brother’s house.
And his name shall be called in Israel: The House of Him Whose Sandal Was Loosed.

verse_units.text: And if brethren dwell together, and one of them dies, and has no seed, the wife of the dead shall not be married outside unto a man who is not near of kin. Her husband’s brother shall go in unto her, and take her unto himself for a wife, and dwell with her as husband.
And it shall be, that the child whom she bears shall be established in the name of the dead, and his name shall not be blotted out of Israel.

And if the man will not take his brother’s wife, the woman shall go up unto the gate, unto the elders, and say: My husband’s brother will not raise up his brother’s name in Israel; my husband’s brother has refused.
And the elders of his city shall call him, and speak unto him; and if he stands and says: I will not take her,

then his brother’s wife shall draw near before the elders, and loose one sandal from his foot, and spit in his face, and answer and say: Thus shall they do unto the man who will not build up his brother’s house.
And his name shall be called in Israel: The House of Him Whose Sandal Was Loosed.

Original scope: Original recipient: Israel at the covenant assembly. Record type: Covenant exhortation; continuity review open. Joshua calls Israel to exclusive allegiance. Read the renewed covenant and the people’s response before applying the passage; this entry is not an additional count of the Torah’s prohibition of idolatry.
Full research entry

verses.text:
Now fear the Lord and serve Him with uprightness and righteousness. Remove the foreign gods your fathers served beyond the River and in Egypt, and serve the Lord.
But if it does not please you to serve the Lord, choose for yourselves today whom you will serve: the gods of your fathers beyond the River, or the gods of the Amorites in whose land you dwell. But I and my house will serve the Lord, for He is holy.”
The people answered and said, “May it never be that we abandon the Lord to serve other gods.
The Lord our God—He is God. He brought us and our fathers up from Egypt and guarded us on all the way we travelled and among all the nations through whom we passed.
The Lord drove out before us the Amorites and all the nations living in the land. We too will serve the Lord, for He is our God.”
Joshua said to the people, “You cannot serve the Lord, for He is a holy God; and being jealous, He will not forgive your sins and your lawless deeds.
Whenever you forsake the Lord and serve other gods, He shall come upon you and afflict you and consume you in return for the good He has done you.”
The people said to Joshua, “No! We will serve the Lord.”
And Joshua said to the people, “You are witnesses against yourselves that you have chosen the Lord to serve Him.
Now remove the foreign gods among you and direct your heart to the Lord, the God of Israel.”
The people said to Joshua, “The Lord we will serve, and His voice we will obey.”

verse_units.text: Now fear the Lord and serve Him with uprightness and righteousness. Remove the foreign gods your fathers served beyond the River and in Egypt, and serve the Lord.

But if it does not please you to serve the Lord, choose for yourselves today whom you will serve: the gods of your fathers beyond the River, or the gods of the Amorites in whose land you dwell. But I and my house will serve the Lord, for He is holy.”
The people answered and said, “May it never be that we abandon the Lord to serve other gods.
The Lord our God—He is God. He brought us and our fathers up from Egypt and guarded us on all the way we travelled and among all the nations through whom we passed.
The Lord drove out before us the Amorites and all the nations living in the land. We too will serve the Lord, for He is our God.”
Joshua said to the people, “You cannot serve the Lord, for He is a holy God; and being jealous, He will not forgive your sins and your lawless deeds.
Whenever you forsake the Lord and serve other gods, He shall come upon you and afflict you and consume you in return for the good He has done you.”
The people said to Joshua, “No! We will serve the Lord.”
And Joshua said to the people, “You are witnesses against yourselves that you have chosen the Lord to serve Him.
Now remove the foreign gods among you and direct your heart to the Lord, the God of Israel.”
The people said to Joshua, “The Lord we will serve, and His voice we will obey.”

nor by the earth, for it is the footstool of His feet, nor by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King.
Nor shall you swear by your head, for you cannot make one hair white or black.
But let your word be ‘Yes, yes’; ‘No, no.’ Whatever is beyond these is of evil.

You have heard that it was said: ‘You shall love your neighbour and hate your enemy.’
But I tell you: love your enemies, and pray for those who persecute you,
that you may become sons of your Father who is in the heavens; for He makes His sun rise upon the evil and the good, and sends rain upon the righteous and the unrighteous.
For if you love those who love you, what reward do you have? Do not even the tax collectors do the same?
And if you greet only your brothers, what are you doing beyond others? Do not even the Gentiles do the same?
You shall therefore be perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect.

verses.text:
Calling the crowd to Him again, He said to them, “Listen to Me, all of you, and understand.
There is nothing outside a person that, by entering him, can defile him. Rather, the things coming out of a person are what defile the person.”
When He entered a house away from the crowd, His disciples asked Him about the parable.
He said to them, “Are you also so lacking in understanding? Do you not grasp that everything entering a person from outside cannot defile him,
because it does not enter his heart but his stomach, and goes out into the latrine?”—thus cleansing all foods.
He said, “What comes out of a person is what defiles the person.
For from within, out of people’s hearts, come evil reasonings, acts of sexual immorality, thefts, murders,
adulteries, acts of greed, wickedness, deceit, licentiousness, an evil eye, slander, arrogance, foolishness.
All these evil things come out from within and defile the person.”

verses.text:
“If anyone comes to Me and does not hate his own father and mother and wife and children and brothers and sisters, and even his own life, he cannot be My disciple.
Whoever does not carry his own cross and come after Me cannot be My disciple.
For which of you, wanting to build a tower, does not first sit down and calculate the expense, whether he has enough to finish it?
Otherwise, when he has laid a foundation and is unable to complete it, all who see it may begin to mock him,
saying, ‘This man began to build and was unable to finish.’
Or what king, going to meet another king in war, will not first sit down and consider whether he is able with ten thousand to meet the one coming against him with twenty thousand?
And if not, while the other is still far away, he sends a delegation and asks for terms of peace.
So, therefore, every one of you who does not renounce all his own possessions cannot be My disciple.

For David says concerning Him, ‘I kept the Lord before me always, for He is at my right hand so that I will not be shaken.
Therefore my heart rejoiced and my tongue exulted; moreover, my flesh will dwell in hope,
because Thou wilt not abandon my soul to Hades, nor allow Thy Holy One to see decay.
Thou hast made known to me the paths of life; Thou wilt fill me with gladness in Thy presence.’
Men, brothers, I may speak openly to you about the patriarch David: he both died and was buried, and his tomb is among us to this day.
Since he was a prophet and knew that God had sworn an oath to him to seat one from the fruit of his loins upon his throne,
he foresaw and spoke about the resurrection of the Christ: He was neither abandoned to Hades, nor did His flesh see decay.
God raised this Jesus, and all of us are witnesses of it.

verses.text:
For I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, that our fathers were all under the cloud and all passed through the sea,
and all were baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea,
and all ate the same spiritual food,
and all drank the same spiritual drink, for they drank from a spiritual rock that followed them, and the rock was Christ.
But God was not pleased with most of them, for they were strewn over the wilderness.
Now these things became examples for us, so that we might not desire evil things as they also desired.
Do not become idolaters, as some of them did, just as it is written: “The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose to play.”
Nor let us commit sexual immorality, as some of them did, and twenty-three thousand fell in one day.
Nor let us put Christ to the test, as some of them tested Him and were being destroyed by the serpents.
Nor grumble, just as some of them grumbled and were destroyed by the destroyer.
These things happened to them as examples, and were written to admonish us, upon whom the ends of the ages have arrived.

What I mean is this: the law, which came four hundred and thirty years later, does not invalidate a covenant previously ratified by God, so as to nullify the promise.
For if the inheritance is from law, it is no longer from promise. But God has graciously given it to Abraham through promise.

Endure for discipline. God deals with you as sons; for what son is there whom a father does not discipline?
But if you are without discipline, in which all have become partakers, then you are illegitimate children and not sons.
Furthermore, we had our fathers in the flesh to discipline us, and we respected them. But shall we not much more submit to the Father of spirits and live?

Now every discipline seems for the present to be a matter of sorrow, not joy, but afterward it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness to those trained through it.

And the Lord said to Moses, “Rise early in the morning, and stand before Pharaoh, and you shall say to him, ‘Thus says the Lord, the God of the Hebrews: Let My people go, that they may serve Me.
For at this time I will send all My blows upon your heart, and upon your attendants and your people, that you may know that there is none other like Me in all the earth.
For now I will stretch out My hand and strike you and your people with death, and you shall be blotted out from the earth.
And for this reason you were preserved, that I might show My strength in you, and that My name might be proclaimed throughout all the earth.
Do you still act against My people, refusing to let them go?
At this time tomorrow I will rain down very abundant hail, such as has never been in Egypt from the day it was created until today.
Now therefore hurry to gather your livestock, and all that you have in the plain; for all the men and livestock found in the plain, who have not entered a house, shall die when the hail falls upon them.’”

The Lord said to Moses, “Go to Pharaoh, for I have hardened his heart and his attendants’ hearts, so that these signs may come upon them in succession,
that you may tell in the ears of your children, and of your children’s children, how I have mocked the Egyptians, and My signs which I have performed among them; and you shall know that I am the Lord.”
And Moses and Aaron went in before Pharaoh, and said to him, “Thus says the Lord, the God of the Hebrews: How long will you refuse to reverence Me? Let My people go, that they may serve Me.
But if you will not let My people go, behold, at this hour tomorrow I will bring many locusts upon all your borders.
And they shall cover the face of the land, and you shall not be able to see the land; and they shall devour all that remains of the land which the hail left to you, and every tree growing for you upon the land.
And your houses shall be filled, and the houses of your attendants, and all the houses throughout the land of the Egyptians, as neither your fathers nor their forefathers have ever seen, from the day they came upon the earth to this day.” And Moses turned and went out from Pharaoh.

He says to him again a second time, “Simon, son of John, do you love Me?” He says to Him, “Yes, Lord, Thou knowest that I love Thee.” He says to him, “Shepherd My sheep.”
